summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package declares a postinstall script that runs beacon.cjs, and its main entrypoint invokes the same beacon on require(). beacon.cjs POSTs installer-side host identifiers — hostname, current working directory, install path, Node.js version, and package name — to the hardcoded plain-HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc, a bare IP unrelated to any npm publisher infrastructure. The package otherwise exposes no real functionality: it self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and its main module exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any accessed property, so the only effective behavior on install or import is the beacon callback. The combination of a scoped lookalike name, no advertised functionality, hardcoded bare-IP exfiltration destination, and dual install- and import-time triggers matches a dependency-confusion / name-squat reconnaissance payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
